stories.headline: Mitchell robs Padres of tying homer as Brewers clinch NLDS
stories.summary: Garrett Mitchell robbed the Padres' Manny Machado of a potential game-tying home run in the eighth inning, and the Brewers advanced to the NLCS for the second straight season with a 3-1 win in Game 4.
stories.body:
SAN DIEGO -- Garrett Mitchell tripled and scored the tiebreaking run in the fifth inning before making a pivotal catch on Manny Machado's drive to the wall in the eighth, and the Milwaukee Brewers advanced to the National League Championship Series for the second straight season with a 3-1 victory over the San Diego Padres on Wednesday night, winning their best-of-five Division Series in four games.

Mitchell also drove in Sal Frelick with Milwaukee's first run as the Brewers snapped their 12-game postseason road losing streak since 2018 and reached the team's fifth League Championship Series.

Machado nearly tied Game 4 with a 406-foot drive off reliever Abner Uribe, but Mitchell coolly tracked it down and reached just above the short wall in right-center to keep it in the yard.

Second baseman Brice Turang then ended the eighth with an acrobatic catch of Ty France's tailing popup in foul ground.

After fending off the surging Padres in four tight games decided by a combined five runs, the 103-win Brewers will get an NLCS rematch with the Los Angeles Dodgers, who eliminated Atlanta on Wednesday.

The Dodgers swept Milwaukee last October on the way to their second consecutive World Series title.

Fernando Tatis Jr. hit a 429-foot homer on an otherwise tepid offensive night for the Padres, who repeatedly tested the majors' best regular-season team before falling short of only the fourth NLCS appearance in team history.

One night after the Padres avoided elimination in Game 3, Milwaukee claimed its first road playoff win since the 2018 NLCS by sticking to its season-long formula for success.

While four Brewers pitchers combined on a three-hitter and the defense made nearly every big play, Milwaukee's lineup calmly worked counts, pounded 10 hits through the Padres' defense and manufactured enough runs to head home smiling.

Game 2 hero Jackson Chourio capped his high-impact series by driving in Mitchell to become the Brewers' career leader in postseason RBI at just 22 years old. Chourio has 17 RBI, including six in this series, in 16 playoff games.

Milwaukee opened the scoring in the third when Frelick reached on an infield single, stole second and came around on a single by Mitchell, an Orange County native and UCLA product.

Brewers starter and former Padres draft pick Robert Gasser threw four innings of three-hit ball, but Tatis ended his 1-for-19 skid since San Diego's playoff opener with a long shot to center in the third. It was the longest homer ever hit in the postseason at Petco Park by a San Diego player.

Padres starter Walker Buehler yielded just three hits and a run, but manager Craig Stammen replaced him with Game 1 starter Robbie Ray after William Contreras' leadoff single in the fourth.

Mitchell then stroked a mild liner perfectly over first base and into the right-field corner leading off the fifth, and he scored on Chourio's single through the drawn-in infield. Chourio surpassed Ryan Braun for the most postseason RBI in Brewers history.

Jake Bauers singled leading off the sixth and went to third on Cooper Pratt's ground-rule double before scoring on Frelick's sacrifice fly.

The Padres were already down 3-1 in the seventh when Mason Miller allowed three baserunners, but no runs. The vaunted closer missed Game 3 for the birth of his first child.

After sitting below .500 and in 11th place in the NL in late July, San Diego roared into the first wild-card spot and then swept the Cubs in the Wild Card Series last week. The Padres had won 19 of 22 before losing three of four to Milwaukee.

The Brewers host the Dodgers in Game 1 on Sunday with ace Jacob Misiorowski almost certainly lined up to start. Milwaukee is four wins from only the second World Series berth in team history.

stories.headline: 2026 WNBA playoffs: How the Valkyries and Dream took 2-0 leads in the semis
stories.summary: Atlanta needed extra time. Golden State took care of business (barely!) in regulation. Now they're one win away from the Finals.
stories.body:
The Atlanta Dream needed extra time. The Golden State Valkyries took care of business (barely!) in regulation.

Now both teams are a win away from advancing to the WNBA Finals.

The No. 4 seed Dream beat the No. 8 seed New York Liberty 101-98 in overtime on Wednesday to take a 2-0 lead in their WNBA playoff semifinal series. In the nightcap, No. 2 Golden State held off the No. 3 Las Vegas Aces 83-81 in San Francisco to put the defending WNBA champions on the brink of elimination.

Both best-of-five series shift, with New York and Las Vegas hosting must-win games Friday. The Liberty host the Dream at 7:30 p.m. ET (ESPN2) at Barclays Center; the Aces host the Valkyries in Game 3 at Michelob ULTRA Arena at 9:30 p.m. ET.

Atlanta played Wednesday without injured starting guard Allisha Gray, who suffered an injury to her left (shooting) hand in Game 1. She is day-to-day.

ESPN was courtside in Atlanta and the Bay Area to break down how the Dream beat the Liberty despite 35 points from Breanna Stewart, and how a two-year-old franchise handed the Aces just their fourth back-to-back losses of this season.

MORE: Game 1 analysis | Playoff schedule

(2) Golden State Valkyries 83,

(3) Las Vegas Aces 81

How Golden State won the game: The Valkyries are making a habit of having a different player off the bench change the game on any given night. In Game 2, it was Tiffany Hayes. The veteran guard finished with a team-high 21 points on 8-of-10 shooting.

Golden State's depth can hide off nights from its stars. Veronica Burton, who was benched in the third quarter of Game 1, finished with just eight points Wednesday. But another big night from Gabby Williams -- 20 points, with three 3-pointers -- and 18 points from Kayla Thornton helped compensate for Burton.

The Valkyries held a 16-point lead midway through the second quarter, but the Aces managed to cut it to eight by halftime. Then Golden State built another lead in the third -- this time by 17. Once again, the Aces chipped away. In the fourth quarter, Las Vegas found new life and took the lead with about 90 seconds left. A'ja Wilson and Chelsea Gray combined for 43 points in the game, but the Valkyries had just enough left to secure the win.

Even though the Aces made it a game, the control the Valkyries took early was a direct carryover from how they played Game 1. Their defense set the tone -- and everything else followed.

What it means for Golden State: The Valkyries are one win away from advancing to the WNBA Finals for the first time in franchise history. That's especially impressive given Golden State only joined the league ahead of the 2025 season. But to do it against the defending champions would be otherworldly. The Valkyries can sweep the Aces if they capture Game 3.

Keys to Game 3: The Aces need more scoring, more defense, more effort. Heading into Game 2, they were adamant they would up their level of physicality and make the Valkyries feel them. But they failed to do so. They finally got production from players other than Wilson and Gray -- Jackie Young finished with 14 points and Stephanie Talbot had 10 in her first game back. Yes, they balled back from a 17-point deficit to take the lead late. But it took too long for them to find what worked. If Vegas wants to stave off elimination, the Aces need to punch first -- because working from behind hasn't been successful in this series. -- Kendra Andrews

(4) Atlanta Dream 101,

(8) New York Liberty 98 OT

How Atlanta won the game: New York shot 55% from the field but it wasn't enough to get the win because it had so many fewer possessions or chances, taking 20 fewer shots than the Dream. Turnovers continued to plague the Liberty in Game 2, and the Dream capitalized, scoring 28 points off 17 turnovers -- no miscue as detrimental as when Sabrina Ionescu sailed a pass out of bounds toward the end of overtime with the Liberty down one. Jordin Canada won the battle of the point guards, scoring or assisting on 45 of Atlanta's 101 points.

Stewart did all she could, particularly in the first half, scoring 25 of New York's 54 points -- the second most in a first half of a WNBA playoff game. But the Liberty barely got any offensive contributions outside of Stewart, Jonquel Jones (21) and Marine Fauthoux (20). Fauthoux's heroics -- a massive 3-pointer -- forced overtime. Atlanta had a balanced effort with six players scoring in double figures, tying a Dream franchise playoff record. That included Isobel Borlase off the bench with 11 points.

The Liberty also were hurt by shooting 16-for-23 from the free throw line. The Dream were much more accurate by making 21 of 23 attempts.

In overtime, it felt like the first team to make a mistake would lose, and that ended up being New York: The Dream forced a jump ball with 11.7 seconds left after collapsing on Jones. Then Ionescu's bad turnover on an ensuing drive after the Liberty retained possession sealed New York's fate.

What it means for the Dream: Atlanta takes a commanding 2-0 lead to Brooklyn. The Dream now have three chances to win the series and advance to their first Finals since 2013. Throughout WNBA history, teams that take a 2-0 lead of a best-of-five series have a series record of 19-0.

Keys to Game 3: Can the Liberty stop committing turnovers and letting the Dream convert them? Can someone slow Canada? Back on their home floor and in front of their raucous fans, can the Liberty play with some pride to avoid a sweep? -- Alexa Philippou

stories.headline: Giants' Malik Nabers has 'sore' knee, doesn't practice
stories.summary: Giants star wide receiver Malik Nabers did not practice Wednesday because of a knee injury, saying only he was more "sore" than usual.
stories.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- New York Giants star wide receiver Malik Nabers did not practice Wednesday because of a knee injury, saying only he was more "sore" than usual.

He exited the Giants' first practice of the week Wednesday and sat on a medicine ball and talked to team trainers during the open portion of practice. The Pro Bowl receiver seemed to be walking with a slight limp when the two-hour practice was over.

"Just sore," Nabers said at the podium moments later. "Just sore. We'll see how the next day goes, but through the week, I'm usually sore. But this one was kind of a little bit more sore. I always continue to fight through it."

The Giants could use him in the lineup for Sunday's game against the Washington Commanders after already having lost Braxton Berrios to a season-ending foot injury.

Nabers tore the ACL in his right knee last season and needed a cleanup procedure earlier this year. He returned to the practice field for the start of training camp and was ready for the opener.

He had his most productive game since returning from the injury Sunday when he caught six passes on seven targets for 112 yards and a touchdown in a win over the Arizona Cardinals.

Coach John Harbaugh didn't seem too worried about his No. 1 receiver.

"He's doing great, yeah," Harbaugh said. "He had a great day. Great spirits [Wednesday]. He had a good workday."

When told that Nabers said he was sore, Harbaugh barely flinched.

"I'll take him at his word then," he said.

Nabers isn't the Giants' only injury concern. Defensive lineman Chauncey Golston has a recurring neck problem that Harbaugh said "could" shut him down for significant time. The Giants and Golston are exploring all their options.

Nabers, who leads the Giants with 208 receiving yards this season, talked just last week about gaining more trust in his knee. He admitted at the start of the season that he was rusty, and he failed to reach 100 yards through the first three games.

He seemed to know that a breakout game was coming. On Sunday, it still wasn't enough for his liking when the Giants and starting quarterback Jameis Winston fed him the ball. Nabers was seen at times animatedly talking toward the sideline from the field. He thought they left some out there.

"I felt like I didn't get targeted much after halftime," said Nabers, who had one catch on two targets for 28 yards in the second half. "So, that was just a thing. It's just ... I felt like creating explosives down the field was just helping us get in a better position to score touchdowns. Some of those plays didn't come my way, so just trying to figure out why."

Harbaugh said they talked after the game, brushing it off as Nabers being emotional and competitive.

"Yeah, I talked to him just about ... I think we need to implement more things after halftime," Nabers said. "Just also trying to give me the ball down the field to create some of those opportunities for us to gain more points. It felt like during the first half when we did that, it kind of led into the right direction with scoring touchdowns in the red zone. And just, after that, we just couldn't get going.

"So, I felt like the offense was needing a spark and I wanted to be that spark. So I was just trying to figure out what was going on, and what was the thought process after halftime."

stories.headline: How Jason Sudeikis and 'Ted Lasso' became champions for women's soccer
stories.summary: The cast of the hit comedy as well as NWSL veterans reflect on bringing authentic stories of women's soccer to a new stage.
stories.body:
JUNO TEMPLE HARDLY let the question breathe before answering it.

It was posed to her, Emmy winner Hannah Waddingham and Jeremy Swift, who star in the hit Apple TV show "Ted Lasso" -- Temple as model-turned-businesswoman Keeley Jones, Waddingham as fictional AFC Richmond owner Rebecca Welton and Swift as director of communications and football operations Leslie Higgins.

Why does women's football work in "Ted Lasso" at this moment?

"Why wouldn't it?" Temple said.

She beat Waddingham to it.

"Yeah, why wouldn't it?" Waddingham jumped in. "Why wouldn't it?"

Women's soccer in the United States and around the world has never been so popular.

The sport has been on an upward trajectory for more than a decade and doesn't look to be slowing down anytime soon. According to a report by Nielsen in 2025, women's soccer is set to become one of the world's top five sports by 2030 with a global fan base of 800 million with about 60% of those fans projected to be women.

In the NWSL, the growth has been constant since it was established in 2013 with eight teams. It had 16 teams during the 2026 season with two more to be added by 2028. In the past five years, the entry fee for a franchise has skyrocketed from $2 million in 2021 to $205 million in 2026. But, wait, there's more. The entry fee grew $40 million between the 17th team and the 18th team. Salaries have also grown from $6,000 a year in 2013 to a league-record $2 million, which went to Trinity Rodman of the Washington Spirit in January. Viewership, attendance and retail sales were all up at the midway point of the 2026 season, with leaguewide retail sales jumping 72% from last year.

"Everything is just progressing in the upward direction and it's growing and we're expanding the league," Angel City midfielder Nealy Martin told ESPN. "And, yeah, I think it's a great time to invest in women's sports, even in the entertainment space."

According to veteran Gotham FC midfielder Meredith Speck, the league is unrecognizable from where it was when she joined the league in 2016.

When Speck heard that the hit Apple show was going to return for a fourth season with the beloved fictional football-turned-soccer coach managing a second-division women's team, she was torn.

On one hand, she knew how wholesome, heartwarming and funny the show was in its first three seasons, when Jason Sudeikis' titular character managed a men's team. And she knew having a storyline that was written specifically about her sport would give it even more exposure than it already receives.

"I was excited because I do love 'Ted Lasso,'" Speck told ESPN. "I had faith."

Can a comedy accurately capture the realities of women's soccer?
On the other hand, she was worried how this season would portray women's soccer.

"I was a little nervous about how it was going to be received because I didn't want it to feel like such a parody," Speck said. "Now, looking at the league, it is serious and professional and women can. ... It's their livelihood.

"So, I was a little nervous."

None of her concerns dissipated as she started watching this season. After the first two episodes, she noticed that the show was just as wholesome, heartwarming and funny as it was during the first three seasons, but it was also accurate in its depiction of women's soccer.

A little too accurate, in fact.

"I'm like, 'These jokes feel very close to home,'" said Speck.

There was the scene in the second episode of this season when Lasso sees the women's locker room for the first time and notices there's just one showerhead. Or the scenes from early in the series that highlighted the differences between the men's and women's locker rooms. Or when Waddingham's character drunkenly asks, "Where are you?" to absent supporters of the Lady Greyhounds -- which brought Speck back to Megan Rapinoe's speech after her final NWSL home game, which set an attendance record at the time, when Rapinoe said: "I hope to see all of you at all the home games next year."

Each scene brought back a memory for Speck of the early days of her NWSL career and it got her wondering if the league's rookies would understand some of the references and jokes in the show.

"They're like, 'I don't get it. What is the scene about our locker room having no showers?'" Speck said. "And I'm like, 'Well, of course you don't get that joke. That's not your reality.'"

Early in the season, Speck continued to worry that viewers would think some of those situations were just written for a comedic impact.

"I hope that people don't just laugh this off because it's not so far from the reality," said Speck, who attended the red carpet for the show's premiere in New York.

Seven episodes and most of a story arc later and heading into Wednesday's season finale of "Ted Lasso," Speck's concern and nerves about the show are finally gone.

"I think, now, having been caught up, I love it and I love that they've chosen to highlight women's soccer," Speck said. "And I think that they've done it in a really thoughtful, careful way, and I've been thrilled watching."

Why did the creators decide to pivot to the women's game for the latest season?
MONTHS AFTER THE Season 3 finale aired in May 2023 -- open-ended and full of breadcrumbs, leaving fans yearning for more and speculating about where the story of the beloved coach would go next (if it went anywhere) -- Sudeikis, the writer and star, and his costars started throwing out potential ideas for the next chapter of the Emmy-winning show.

One was spin-offs. Another was Lasso coaching a Major League Soccer team. And part of that idea was Welton buying MLS side Sporting KC.

"These are all things [we thought about]," Brendan Hunt, who plays Lasso's righthand man, assistant coach Willis Beard, told ESPN. "So, yeah, this was potentially parallel universe and not definitively what we would come back and do if we were going to come back."

And that's where the future of "Ted Lasso" began to formulate.

Yet, through all the ideas, all the possibilities, Sudeikis felt that in order to bring back the immensely popular show, he'd have to have a good reason.

"I felt we had done, we all felt, I think, behind the scenes, that we had told that first story as I was hoping we would tell it," Sudeikis told ESPN. "And, so, it was like, OK, well to come back, it has to be for some other reason.

"So what could that be?"

Sudeikis kept coming back to one storyline in particular -- one that was teed up by Temple's character, who, in the final minutes of the Season 3 finale, as Cat Stevens' "Father and Son" plays in the background, hands Waddingham's character a binder, inside of which is a plan for the AFC Richmond women's team.

Abbie Hern, who plays prolific goal scorer Gemma Jay, doesn't like to watch series finales. That way the shows never end, she said. So, it wasn't until she got the role in "Ted Lasso" that she watched the last episode of Season 3 and when Temple handed Waddingham the binder, Hern knew where she and the other new actors fit in.

"We just loved these characters so much and we got to know them so well," Sudeikis said. "But, it was like, 'Oh, if, if.' But I just love the idea. We love the idea of Keeley bringing this to Rebecca."

Sudeikis knew one thing, though, if Ted Lasso were to continue in any way, shape or form: He wanted it to be in the world of women's soccer.

So, when the decision was made to not just write a fourth season but to pivot the entire storyline to women's soccer, Sudeikis said his costars were quickly and entirely on board.

"It was yes by a thousand cuts is the way I've been trying to describe it," Sudeikis said.

"F--- yeah, quite frankly," Waddingham said was her reaction. "Yeah, about time, too."

How is 'Ted Lasso' helping women's soccer achieve true parity?
Then, in August, came this season of "Ted Lasso."

Along with the show came a record number of eyes on women's soccer. The show's Season 4 premiere drew 296.6 million minutes watched Aug. 4-5, according to Variety, making it the biggest debut in Apple TV's history. Nielsen reported that the first episode of Season 4 on Aug. 5 was watched for more than 200 million minutes, making it the most streamed program in the U.S. that day.

And that meant that during those 200 million minutes from the first episode, viewers saw footage from CPKC Stadium, the only venue in the country dedicated to women's soccer, and home to the NWSL's Kansas City Current. When Temple and other castmates were at the stadium for a press conference in July, she was so overwhelmed by being in a women's-soccer-specific stadium that she was brought to tears.

"I feel like football in general, especially in America, has become more of a thing," Temple said. "We grew up in England. It's a religion there. But, I think in this day and age, I think being able to embrace women's football in the way that people embrace men's football, it may take a little longer, but it's important that we're open to it.

"I mean, it's ridiculous that it wouldn't be considered to be a great storyline."

Washington Spirit center back Tara Rudd said coming off the men's FIFA World Cup this summer was the perfect time for "Ted Lasso" to be released to help segue the soccer conversation back to the women's game. Having her sport and, to a degree, her league, be showcased to a global audience has been "huge," Rudd said.

Sofia Huerta, a right back for Seattle Reign FC, has been a "Ted Lasso" fan since the beginning and believes the show brings new fans to the NWSL.

"I think for the NWSL, it will be good because there's going to be people who are fans of the show and then maybe they'll recognize the NWSL and then they'll fall in love with the way that we play in the athletes and atmosphere," Huerta said.

"So, I think it'll just help grow the game immensely, which is exciting."

Faye Marsay, who plays Lizzie Davis, a single mother of two who's a captain of AFC Richmond, grew up playing soccer in England until a knee injury she suffered when she was 16 ended her playing days on the pitch and launched her career on stage. When she played on a girls' team in the late 1990s, she didn't have a pathway to a full-time professional career because one didn't exist. The Women's Super League, the highest level of women's soccer in England, didn't enter its full-time, professional era until the 2018-19 season.

Being part of "Ted Lasso" now, has, in a way, filled in the void that soccer left in her as a teenager -- while also saving her knees.

"It's amazing, but it's also about time," Marsay told ESPN. "So, in a way, it's kind of a bittersweet thing for me because I wish it had been when I was still younger."

She added: "I think using 'Ted Lasso' as the platform to shine a light on and I don't think it's a moment that women's football's having. I think they've always been there. It's just now we're starting to appreciate it. And I think this will only create way more conversations around what we should be doing better."

Seattle Reign manager Laura Harvey, who grew up in England and coached throughout the WSL from 2002 to 2012, when she last managed Arsenal, came of age when movies like "Bend It Like Beckham" exposed soccer to a global audience. She said "Ted Lasso" can have just as positive of an impact on the women's game.

"I think I've always had the mindset that when people see it, that they'll want to come back and watch it," Harvey told ESPN. "I think that is true, still reigns true now."

What does real-world support from figures like Sudeikis and the cast of 'Ted Lasso' mean for the NWSL?
THE WEEKEND AFTER the New York City premiere, Sudeikis, Hunt and a few of the actors who play on AFC Richmond attended Gotham FC's match against San Diego Wave FC and spent some time with the players on the field after the game.

"They were so awesome and so excited to be there, which was just a funny moment because I feel like we were both very appreciative of meeting each other, which was nice," Speck said.

It got to a point that night, that Sudeikis' people had to pull him away from the field because of other obligations. The whole evening left Speck feeling like Sudeikis was as genuine as he came off.

And it's hard to argue that his support for women's sports isn't.

Sudeikis has not been shy about his support of the WNBA, the NWSL and other women's sports and athletes. And having an actor of his caliber from a show with the stature of "Ted Lasso" as an ally of women's sports has been a boost for the league and its players.

"I think it's important because, in reality, women's sports has been neglected for a long time," Huerta said. "And, so, now we're seeing investment from whether that's just the attention from people at that level or companies or businesses who are investing. We're finally getting that attention and the water that we need.

"So, having someone like Jason, it's big time because he's obviously a celebrity and so hopefully there can just be more attention around that. He has a big following. Obviously, that's part of his brand. He's very passionate about women's sports. And so just puts more eyes on the sports, which is really good for us. And I also think it just helps people connect with us because people connect with him, maybe they feel like since he connects with women's sports, that they can connect with us as well and the players and the teams, and then they become more invested. So, it really, really helps us."

Sudeikis said his inspiration to pivot the storyline came from experiences like his and his family's love of the WNBA, and the experience of being in London in 2022 while filming Season 3 when the Lionesses won the UEFA Women's Euro 2022 and then meeting some of the players.

"It just seemed like a natural progression," he said.

Harvey said that for years, the perception was that anyone who publicly supported women's sports did so "as a charity move." That's not the case anymore, she added.

"I think people like Jason and all the other people that are investing their time and effort and money into women's sport are changing the narrative that it's not just a cool and nice thing to do, but it's actually a really smart business move, too," Harvey said.

Sudeikis has a unique ability the others don't: He can bring women's soccer and their stories onto screens in people's homes and hands all over the world.

And he understands the responsibility that comes with that.

Sudeikis said one goal of his with "Ted Lasso" was to make something that was "cool" for the people he looked up to like "Saturday Night Live" head Lorne Michaels; his peers like Kristen Wiig, Bill Hader, Andy Samberg; his mentors Amy Poehler and Tina Fey, and his sisters. He wanted them to think what he creates is funny, cool and uniquely him.

This season of "Ted Lasso" is all about accomplishing that. But there's more. Something bigger than all of them.

"To then have this going into this world that I think is such an incredible space and is getting the attention, it's long overdue, just women's sports in general, you want to do right by them," Sudeikis said. "I want to do right by all those people I just mentioned, too. It's not like you're thinking about that at every keystroke, but when you're making these things, you just want them to watch it.

"They know the difference between it being real and a television show. Everybody all know[s] it's not a documentary, but the little things that I think that we do pull from the real issues and even real plays and things being based on real players, we take a great care and a great responsibility to that and try to go about it as unparasitically as possible and truly try to honor and share our own enthusiasm for it and have that come across on the show. So, I hope that they enjoy it with that enthusiasm that we make it with."

Temple hopes the show's pivot to women's soccer will inspire all women, regardless of age, pronouns, interests, backgrounds or stories to chase their dreams of soccer if that's what they truly want to do.

For Waddingham, the show's global impact, while, yes, it's focused on women's soccer, should expose the sport to everyone -- not just women.

"The huge beam that this show has cast on football in the first place in America is vast," she told ESPN. "So, if you think about that impact that this could have on the women's game, let's fill the stadiums. ...There's a section where Rebecca speaks to the fact that, yes, young girls and women need to go and support women, but moreover, the little boys need to be taken by their dads to the women's game so that there is no divide.

"We're not asking for more. We're asking for parity."

stories.headline: Max Verstappen says F1 paddock 'less stressful' without Christian Horner
stories.summary: Max Verstappen said the F1 paddock is "less stressful" following Christian Horner's exit from the sport because "it is not nice when you constantly have tension between people."
stories.body:
Max Verstappen said the F1 paddock is "less stressful" following Christian Horner's exit from the sport because "it is not nice when you constantly have tension between people."

Despite being sidelined by Red Bull more than a year ago, Horner's possible comeback remains one of the hottest topics in F1.

Horner, 52, has already declared "unfinished business" and recently spoke of his "dream" to lead Ferrari, forcing the Italian giants to declare "full confidence" in team principal Fred Vasseur.

Horner's sparring with counterpart Toto Wolff, and latterly Zak Brown, shaped F1 for much of the past decade as Mercedes, McLaren and Red Bull fought on the biggest stage.

However, Verstappen insisted a potential Horner comeback is not required to reignite a paddock once compared to a "Piranha Club" because of its ferocity.

In an interview with the Press Association, Verstappen said: "To be honest, I like to see that people get on. It is not nice when you constantly have tension between people.

"Of course, from the outside, people like it, but honestly between the teams, it is better when you have just a friendly relationship. It is not as spicy, but I obviously quite like how things are going at the moment, with everyone's behaviour, let's put it like that.

"It is less stressful. We are all leading a stressful life and, when you can take a bit of stress out of it at times, it is good.

"He has shown he did a good job. Of course, people spread a lot of rumours [about Horner's future], and I don't know how much of that is true.

"I don't want to sound rude, but it is also not my problem or concern. He wants to come back, and if there is a good opportunity, I am sure he will do it, but I don't know where that is going to be."

Verstappen put aside his disdain for the sport's regulations to sign a new contract with Red Bull and commit his future to the sport for another four years.

The 72nd win of his career, in Malaysia -- which leaves him behind only Lewis Hamilton (106) and Michael Schumacher (91) -- arrived just days after Fernando Alonso signed a new Aston Martin deal to extend his stay in F1 beyond his 46th birthday.

"Staying here until then would mean I have dedicated more than half of my life to Formula One, and that is probably a bit too much," the 29-year-old Verstappen said. "I have extended for a few more years, and then I will look again and say to myself, 'Can I commit 100 percent?' And if not, or [if] there are other fun things around that deserves more time, then maybe I don't continue. I also want to spend more time at home and see the kids growing up."

Verstappen spoke with other teams -- including McLaren -- before re-signing with Red Bull. But would he be tempted to follow in the footsteps of Schumacher and Hamilton and drive for Ferrari? The tifosi unusually sang Verstappen's name beneath the podium following the Italian Grand Prix last month.

"I only want to win," he said. "I am not a nostalgic type. Do I have a lot of respect for the [Ferrari] brand? Absolutely. But if that means you then commit yourself, and you are driving P5 or P6, what's the point?

"I am very performance-driven, and I have won a lot with this team already. It is a second family at Red Bull, and the challenge of rebuilding is what's driving me."

stories.headline: Silva rises in P4P women's top 10, making most of golden opportunity
stories.summary: After winning UFC women's flyweight title, Silva rises in ESPN's P4P top 10.
stories.body:
The women's flyweight division might be the most stacked weight class in the UFC, and Natalia Silva wears the gold.

Silva was too fast, too precise and too elusive for Wang Cong in the UFC 332 main event on Saturday, and as a result, the 29-year-old from Brazil captured the vacant 125-pound title. She moves up one position to No. 4 in the ESPN women's pound-for-pound rankings.

Silva is one of seven flyweights in the women's top 10. The division with the next most pound-for-pound elites is lightweight, with three fighters in the men's rankings.

The top two fighters on the women's list are Valentina Shevchenko, who vacated the UFC title last month while healing shoulder and back injuries, and Zhang Weili, a two-time former strawweight titlist who last fought at flyweight, in an unsuccessful challenge of Shevchenko in November.

Aside from Silva, there are three other UFC flyweights in the top 10 (Alexa Grasso, Manon Fiorot and Erin Blanchfield), and the rankings also include PFL 125-pounder Dakota Ditcheva.

UFC women's bantamweight champion Kayla Harrison has been missing from these rankings for the past few months because, with no fights since June 2025, she is ineligible. But Harrison will return from neck surgery to defend her title against former two-division champion and consensus GOAT Amanda Nunes at UFC 334 on Nov. 14.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Oct. 7. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Valentina Shevchenko

UFC flyweight

Record: 26-4-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Zhang Weili, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

Shevchenko's dominance came under question in 2022 and 2023, when she went 1-1-1 in a trilogy with Alexa Grasso. Boy, does that feel like a long time ago now. Shevchenko more than reasserted herself as the best flyweight in the world, and then she established herself as the No. 1 woman in the world, period. It wasn't surprising that she beat Zhang, but it was surprising how easy she made it look. Shevchenko is out injured, however, so she has vacated her UFC title, which Natalia Silva captured by beating Wang Cong at UFC 332. When Shevchenko is healed up, she'll be looking to take back the belt.

2. Zhang Weili

UFC flyweight / strawweight

Record: 26-4

Last: L (UD) vs. Valentina Shevchenko, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

It's hard to move up in weight, especially at the highest level. That sounds like it should be obvious, but Zhang had been dominant at 115 pounds for so long, some of us might have taken for granted how big of a challenge moving to 125 would be. UFC 322 was a bad night for Zhang, but she doesn't have many. And if she decides to stay at flyweight, it certainly seems reasonable to believe she'll fare better in the future.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight champion

Previous ranking: 5

Record: 21-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Wang Cong, Oct. 3

Next: TBA

Silva was looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Rose Namajunas at UFC 324. And now she has fulfilled that expectation, beating Wang at UFC 332 to win the belt vacated by injured Valentina Shevchenko. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027.

5. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Previous ranking: 4

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

6. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber in March, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

7. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

8. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Record: 13-3

Last: L (UD) vs. Alexa Grasso, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Fiorot had handled everyone the UFC put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But then, with another title shot within her grasp, Fiorot ran into Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC and lost a competitive fight.

9. Erin Blanchfield

UFC flyweight

Record: 14-2

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Tracy Cortez, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: Oct. 17 vs. Jasmine Jasudavicius

Her rise toward the top of the division was derailed by a March 2024 loss to Manon Fiorot, but Blanchfield bounced back with two straight wins, including one over two-time former strawweight champion Rose Namajunas in November 2024. If she wins her upcoming bout with Jasudavicius, a fellow top-10 flyweight contender, Blanchfield would inch ever closer to a title shot.

10. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

Record: 12-1

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Loopy Godínez, April 11

Next: TBA

If Suarez is still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Godinez, a fellow top-10 strawweight. Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Valentina Shevchenko; 2. Zhang Weili; 3. Mackenzie Dern; 4. Natalia Silva; 5. Cris Cyborg; 6. Alexa Grasso; 7. Manon Fiorot; 8. Dakota Ditcheva; 9. Erin Blanchfield; 10. Tatiana Suarez.

Carlos Contreras Legaspi: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Cyborg; 3. Silva; 4. Zhang; 5. Dern; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Suarez; 9. Fiorot; 10. Blanchfield.

Andrew Davis: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Silva; 5. Dern; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Fiorot; 9. Blanchfield; 10. Suarez.

Dre Waters: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Dern; 5. Silva; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Blanchfield; 9. Fiorot; 10. Suarez.

Jeff Wagenheim: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Silva; 5. Grasso; 6. Dern; 7. Fiorot; 8. Blanchfield; 9. Suarez; 10. Ditcheva.

Men's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Islam Makhachev

UFC welterweight champion

Record: 29-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Ian Machado Garry, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 20-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Dvalishvili

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet. He can prove it by beating Dvalishvili again.

3. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Record: 21-5

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Yan

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. They will fight for a third time at UFC 333.

T-4. Tom Aspinall

UFC heavyweight

Record: 15-3, 1 NC

Last: NC1 vs. Ciryl Gane, Oct. 25, 2025

Next: TBA

You can make a case that Aspinall is the most dynamic, skillful, talented heavyweight the sport has seen. He is dominating opponents in a way that is unmatched. No one can last a round with him. He had hoped to prove his supremacy against Jon Jones, but Jones opted to retire, elevating Aspinall from interim champion. His first defense of the undisputed belt ended anticlimactically, as an eye poke resulted in his UFC 321 fight with Gane being declared a no-contest. Still recovering from the eye injury, Aspinall vacated his title on Sept. 14.

T-4. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

6. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

7. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 28-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Diego Lopes, Jan. 31

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Movsar Evloev

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (38) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. Can he hand Evloev his first loss at UFC 333?

8. Joshua Van

UFC flyweight champion

Record: 18-2

Last: W (UD) vs. Alexandre Pantoja, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Van has been champion since December, but until UFC 331, there were doubters. Van had been handed the belt by default, when his challenge for the title was waved off after 26 seconds because Pantoja dislocated his left elbow. Van went on to defend the title against Tatsuro Taira in May, then faced Pantoja in a rematch at UFC 331. Van produced a clear victory -- his eighth win in a row -- to leave no doubt who rules at 125 pounds.

9. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight champion

Record: 14-2, 1 NC

Last: W (TKO2) vs. Alex Pereira, June 14

Next: Nov. 14 vs. Josh Hokit

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight on the White House lawn. Gane was elevated to undisputed champ after Aspinall, still injured, vacated his title, and the new champ will defend against Hokit at UFC 334.

10. Arman Tsarukyan

UFC lightweight

Record: 24-3

Last: W (KO1) vs. Mauricio Ruffy, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Tsarukyan is right back in the place he was in January 2025 -- on the cusp of a title fight. He withdrew from a challenge of Islam Makhachev one day before UFC 311 because of a back injury, and later in the year he was passed over twice when the UFC was booking lightweight title bouts. But by knocking out Ruffy with an elbow in the first round at UFC 331, Tsarukyan put himself back at the front of the line.

Other fighter receiving votes: Alex Pereira.

stories.headline: AFL player movement tracker: trade requests, free agency latest, who's on the move?
stories.summary: The offseason is upon us which means AFL trades, free agency, and player movement is about to take off. Here's the latest news, whispers, and confirmed deals.
stories.body:
It's AFL player movement season, with trades and free agency set to dominate the month of October. So who is going where? Keep track with our player movement guide here.

When is the AFL trade and free agency window?
The 2026 AFL trade period commences on Monday, October 5 and closes in the evening of Wednesday, October 14.

The free agency window opens and closes a little earlier; it runs from Friday, October 2 until Friday, October 9.

Thursday, Oct. 8
Marshall lands at the Cats

St Kilda have pulled the trigger on a deal to send contracted ruckman Rowan Marshall to Geelong, as the Cats and other rival clubs circle Sydney star Nick Blakey.

Geelong traded pick No.14 in this year's draft for the disenchanted 30-year-old and a third-round selection in 2028 on Thursday afternoon.

New Zealand-born Marshall had requested a move to the Cats for a second straight year after St Kilda recruited Tom De Koning to become their first-choice ruckman.

-- AAP

Wednesday, Oct. 7
Dons defender gets traded to the Cats

After being denied a trade last year, Jordan Ridley got his wish for a fresh start after Essendon and Geelong agreed to a deal on Wednesday.

Geelong gave up utility Jack Bowes, a 2027 first-round pick and 2028 second-round pick to get the 27-year-old Ridley through the door.

Pick No. 60 and a 2028 fourth-round selection will come back to the Cats from the Bombers.

--AAP

Tuesday, Oct. 6
O'Driscoll makes the move over east

Fremantle have traded 24-year-old Nathan O'Driscoll to Richmond in exchange for pick 61 in this year's draft.

The winger played 17 games for the Dockers this season but wasn't selected for the Grand Final.

Monday, Oct. 5
TRADE PERIOD OPENS
Merrett finally becomes a Hawk

After attempting to join Hawthorn last year, Zach Merrett has finally been traded from Essendon to the Hawks.

Hawthorn have sent picks 15, 25 and a 2028 second-round pick in exchange for the 31-year-old.

Merrett leaves the Bombers a week after winning a record-equaling seventh Crichton Medal, three All-Australian blazers, and 274 games.

Pendlebury becomes a Sun

AFL games record holder Scott Pendlebury is officially a Sun after Gold Coast and Collingwood agreed on a trade for the 38-year-old veteran.

Pendlebury, a two-time premiership player, heads to the Suns in exchange for pick No. 65 in this year's draft.

"It's an exciting group here at the SUNS and the opportunity to bring a few different ideas and also learn from a great group of coaches and players is one I'm really looking forward to," Pendlebury told the Suns.

"This side is one I've watched from afar and really admired. I've got a bit of knowledge about the industry so I'm here to play my role and help this squad continue to develop."

Jesse Hogan traded from GWS to Collingwood

Out-of-favour Giants forward Jesse Hogan has made the switch to Collingwood in exchange for pick 75.

The 31-year-old won the Coleman Medal in 2024 but has been unable to recapture his best form at the Giants in the two years since.

Magpies list boss Justin Leppitsch said Hogan would be a valuable addition.

"On behalf of everyone at Collingwood, I'd like to warmly welcome Jesse to Collingwood. Jesse has established himself as one of the competition's premier key forwards and we're excited to see him bring his experience and talent to our club," he said.

"His aerial presence inside forward-50 and his consistency as a goal-kicker make him a genuine threat.

"Like Lachie (Neale), Jesse has a passion to teach the next generation and will make a great addition to our club."

Saturday, Oct. 3
Bulldogs seal free-agency signing of key defender

The Western Bulldogs have finally snagged the key defender they need, securing Adelaide backman Jordon Butts as an unrestricted free agent.

The Bulldogs are set for a bumper AFL trade period headlined by working through a deal for Port Adelaide superstar Zak Butters, ahead of a 2027 season where the club will have high expectations.

But after seeing off Carlton's advances to keep hold of defender Buku Khamis, the Bulldogs have filled a major area of need by adding 26-year-old Butts.

Adelaide will receive a second-round compensation selection, currently pick No.33, in this year's draft.

-- AAP

Friday, Oct. 2
FREE AGENCY OPEN
Three-peat Lion locks in Magpies move

Lachie Neale has sealed his high-profile switch to Collingwood, with Brisbane teasing the dual Brownlow medallist on his way out the door.

The AFL approved Neale signing a three-year deal with the Magpies on Friday afternoon, closing out the first day of free agency.

The 33-year-old ball-winner leaves as an unrestricted free agent after the Lions clinched a third straight flag with their stunning seven-point grand final victory over Fremantle.

-- AAP

Greene on his way to the Cats

Toby Greene will join Geelong as an unrestricted free agent on a three-year deal, re-partnering with former Giants teammate Jeremey Cameron.

The paperwork was lodged to the AFL on Friday morning.

The Giants receive band three compensation for Greene, which is currently pick No. 26 in the upcoming draft.

Greene departs the Giants with his name etched in the club's record books, sitting first in games played for the club with a tally of 282 games, as well as leading the club's all-time goalkicking tally with 450 majors.

Briggs now a Tiger

Richmond has landed GWS ruck Kieren Briggs as an unrestricted free agent.

Briggs' move to the Tigers was confirmed just hours after the free agency window opened on Friday.

Briggs played 88 games for GWS after joining the club as the No.34 pick in the 2018 draft.

Amartey officially joins the Blues

Free agency has opened with a bang, with out-of-favour key forward Joel Amartey committing to Carlton.

Details are still to come on the length of contract, and Sydney's compensation.

Hawthorn father-son recommits despite interest

Calsher Dear has made a shock decision to re-sign with the Hawks for two years, despite being out of favour thorughout 2026.

The 20-year-old has kicked 39 goals from 31 games, but found himself behind Jack Gunston, Mitch Lewis and Mabior Chol. With Gunston signed on and Suns forward Ben King expected to sign with the Hawks as well, there were questions about whether Dear would get enough opportunity at his childhood club.

Hawks list boss Mark McKenzie said the club was "really pleased" that Dear had recommitted.

"He remains an important part of what we are trying to achieve as a club," he said.

"Following his debut season, Calsher showed us all the special talent that he is, but as a key tall at 21 years of age, we've needed to be patient with his progression.

"Having battled several injuries over his first three seasons in the system, we are very excited about what the future holds for Calsher with a strong pre-season under his belt and greater continuity into 2027 and beyond."

Thursday, Oct. 1
Goater set to make cross-city switch

North Melbourne defender Josh Goater is set to join the Hawks after requesting a trade on Thursday.

Having played just 18 games, the 23-year-old had fallen out of favour after an injury-hit run in his time at North.

Premiership Lion requests trade

The Brisbane Lions have confirmed Sam Marshall has requested a trade to St Kilda.

"The Brisbane Lions confirm premiership midfielder Sam Marshall has requested to be traded to St Kilda," the Lions said in a statement.

"Marshall has played 13 games, including the 2025 Premiership, across two seasons since being selected in the first round of the 2024 draft as a graduate of the Youi Brisbane Lions Academy.

"The club respects Marshall's request to be traded, and will work towards facilitating an outcome that best reflects true value to the Brisbane Lions for the 20-year-old."

Tuesday, Sept. 29
Neale informs Lions he intends to join Collingwood

Two-time Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale has told Brisbane he will depart the club as an unrestricted free agent and sign a three-year deal with Collingwood.

Aware that Neale intended to leave at the end of the year, the Lions never offered him a new contract.

The paperwork for the deal is expected to be formalised as early as Friday when the free agency period opens.

Friday, Sept. 25
Jordon Butts to join the Bulldogs

Zak Butters isn't the only South Australian-based player keen to join the Western Bulldogs, with Crows' key defender Jordon Butts officially naming the Dogs as his preferred offseason destination.

The unrestricted free agent will sign a five-year deal at the Kennel, according to AFL.com.au.

Tuesday, Sept. 22
Amartey officially names Carlton

Wantaway Sydney forward Joel Amartey has confirmed his desire to join Carlton as an unrestricted free agent.

The 26-year-old was kept out of the Swans' side with an Achilles injury in the latter stages of the year.

With Charlie Curnow (75 goals in 2026) and Logan McDonald (51) cementing their spots in the Sydney forward line as the prime targets, Amartey is hoping for more opportunity at the Blues.

Thursday, Sept. 17
GWS captain finally makes big call on his future

Toby Greene has opted to leave GWS, telling the AFL club he wishes to play with Geelong next season. Greene, who has been at the Giants since their foundation season in 2012, wants to go back to Victoria for family reasons.

In an extraordinary way to announce the decision, outgoing GWS boss Dave Matthews confirmed Greene's intentions on radio, before the club released a statement.

The 32-year-old has been offered a lucrative three-year deal to join the Cats.

Saturday, Sept. 12
Zak Butters makes huge free agency call
The year's hottest restricted free agent Zak Butters has made a huge call on his future, nominating the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination.

After a year of speculation, with Geelong thought to be the front-runner for the Power star's signature, Butters made the call on Saturday, first reported by AFL.com.au's Callum Twomey.

The deal is reportedly for nine years.

Thursday, Sept. 10
Hogan set to join Pies
GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

Zane Duursma wants to go to Melbourne
The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

Ed Allan re-signs with the Pies

stories.headline: NRL: Spencer Leniu signs with Eels after early Roosters release
stories.summary: Spencer Leniu has signed a four-year deal with Parramatta just days after winning his fourth NRL premiership with the Sydney Roosters.
stories.body:
Spencer Leniu has signed a four-year deal with Parramatta just days after winning his fourth NRL premiership with the Sydney Roosters.

Leniu finished his three-year stint at the Tricolours on a high after a stellar performance in their 19-18 win over Newcastle to secure the 2026 trophy.

The NSW Origin representative added the Roosters' premiership ring to the three he won with Penrith from 2021-2023.

Leniu was granted a release from the final year of his Roosters contract, which will give the club some salary cap reprieve

The hard-hitting forward's Eels contract is reportedly worth more than the $850,000 per year he was making with Easts, where he spent much of his time coming off the bench.

He is expected to play a more active role in blue and gold, leading the line for the Eels' forward pack.

The westward move will see the former Panther reunite with good friend Jarome Luai, but first the pair will both suit up for Toa Samoa at the Rugby League World Cup.

Eels general manager of football Mark O'Neill shared his delight at signing one of the game's "premier enforcers".

"We're thrilled to have Spencer join the Parramatta Eels and become part of what we're building at this club," O'Neill said in a statement.

"He's one of the elite middle forwards in the game and has consistently performed on the biggest stages throughout his career.

The exit of Leniu adds to the exodus of stars from the Roosters premiership lineup.

Angus Crichton and Mark Nawaqanitawase are rugby-bound, Daly Cherry-Evans is joining Hull FC, while Daniel Tupou retired this week after his 307-game career.

Connor Watson, who missed the title decider due to concussion, has signed for a season with St George Illawarra Dragons.

Roosters coach Trent Robinson said Leniu had been a strong contributor during his time at the club.

"Spencer has brought a lot to our group over the last three years, both through the way he plays and the energy and personality he brings every day," Robinson said in a statement on Thursday.

"He brings an intensity and competitiveness to everything he does, and he challenges the people around him to be better.

"To see him finish his time here as a premiership winner is something he should be really proud of, and something we'll always share together."

With his departure announced at the Roosters' awards night on Wednesday, Leniu said he would leave the club on a high.

""I'm proud to have worn the Roosters jersey and I'll always have a lot of love and respect for the club, the boys and everyone who has supported me during my time here," said Leniu.

"Winning a premiership with this group and sharing that with the boys, our families and everyone at the club is something I'll carry with me for the rest of my life."

stories.headline: Rays complete sweep of Yankees to advance to ALCS
stories.summary: Victor Mesa Jr. hit the home run that effectively ended the Yankees' season Wednesday night as the Rays won 4-3 to complete a sweep that affirmed Tampa Bay's summer-long dominance of their division rival.
stories.body:
When Victor Mesa Jr. hit the home run that effectively ended the New York Yankees' season Wednesday night, the contact was so pure, the Tampa Bay Rays outfielder explained later, that he didn't even really feel the ball off the bat.

He just knew that he hit it a long, long way, and so rather than watch his work disappear deep into the right-field stands at Yankee Stadium, he immediately turned at home plate and looked toward the dugout to watch his teammates celebrate.

Tampa Bay is moving on to the AL Championship Series, to play the winner of the Cleveland Guardians-Chicago White Sox series, winning 4-3 to complete a sweep of the Yankees that affirmed the Rays' summer-long dominance of their division rival.

Over the span of three games, Tampa Bay's pitching surrendered five runs, stifling the New York lineup, from Drew Rasmussen's near no-hitter in Game 1 to Bryan Baker's series-clinching strikeout.

"The way our pitchers executed as they navigated through that lineup was really impressive," Rays manager Kevin Cash said.

"They beat us," conceded Yankees manager Aaron Boone. "They obviously had a great season."

Cash said his team, which sports one of the lowest payrolls in the majors, isn't out to prove anything to anybody. But Mesa is just another Rays discovery, another example of how they acquired a fringe player and, with their organizational magic, helped foster more than expected. Mesa signed with the Marlins in 2019 and stalled in the Miami organization, playing 16 big league games before he was traded to Tampa Bay last February for infielder Angel Brachi.

He started this season in the minor leagues, and what the Rays learned first-hand about Mesa, after he was called up to the big leagues at the end of May, was that he is steeped with confidence, loves to talk, and can flat out hit.

"He showed he's a really good player as soon as he got here," Rays shortstop Taylor Walls said.

And the left-handed hitter demonstrated a special ability to hit against left-handed pitchers: He batted .333 against lefties during the regular season, almost 100 points higher than what he hit against right-handers.

With Tampa Bay needing one more victory to complete a sweep in Game 3, Mesa was in the lineup against Yankees veteran lefty Max Fried. Cash mused before the game about how Mesa has an ability to slash fastballs off left-handers to left field, but also to pull hanging breaking balls.

The Rays and Yankees were tied 2-all through five innings. Fried's pitch count was over 70 and he was nearing the end of his night in the top of the sixth, when reliever Paul Blackburn started to warm up in the Yankees' bullpen. Fried struck out Yandy Diaz and coaxed Jonathan Aranda into a fly out to center field. When Junior Caminero lashed a ground ball through the middle, Fried dropped to the ground in an effort to avoid the ball as it bounced into center field.

Mesa was the next hitter. Blackburn was ready, if needed, and there were numbers that supported a switch to the right-handed reliever. But Boone stuck with Fried, whose first pitch to Mesa was a sweeper.

A hanger.

Mesa swung viciously, the ball soaring to right field, before turning toward the other Rays in their dugout.

"That's the stage you dream of," he said. "That's the moment you want to live when you're growing up."

Some Rays in the dugout lifted their arms in celebration and whooped.

"I was like, Dude, please go," Walls said. In this case, the Dude was the ball.

Cash pointed at Mesa, still standing at home plate, and screamed: "Run!"

Later, Cash explained with a grin, "The last thing we really need to do is ignite a really good team," referring to the Yankees.

The Yankees would tie the score, ever so briefly, when Anthony Volpe clubbed a ball toward the stands, over Mesa's head and into the outstretched arms of a Yankees fan reaching onto the field. But upon review, fan interference was called and Volpe was placed at second base.

The Yankees never could generate the tying run, and after Baker whiffed Trent Grisham to end the game, the Rays joyfully bounded around the infield, before gathering for a team photo that was briefly delayed as Mesa rushed through the last question of his postgame interviews.

"I gotta go," he said, running off to join his teammates. They have places to go.

stories.headline: Tyrese Haliburton scores 7 in 1st game in more than 16 months
stories.summary: Pacers star Tyrese Haliburton scored seven points during his 16 minutes of action against the Wolves on Wednesday. It was his first game in more than 16 months, as Haliburton was recovering from a torn Achilles.
stories.body:
AMES, Iowa -- Pacers star Tyrese Haliburton said he felt like he was playing too fast during Indiana's 123-112 victory over the Minnesota Timberwolves in its preseason opener at Iowa State on Wednesday night, Haliburton's first game in more than 16 months.

He scored seven points on 3-of-8 shooting with six assists, one steal and two blocks during his 16 minutes of action.

"It's the first game, but it's got to slow down," Haliburton said Wednesday night. "There was just a lot of adrenaline. I was hyped to be out there, excited, but I just got to slow down a little bit."

Haliburton compared himself to a rookie after the game, but he took solace in the fact that although his body was moving too fast, he felt like he could read the floor at his usual speed.

"It'll happen with time," he said. "The only way to really replicate that is game reps against other guys. And that's what that was. So really excited about it.

"There's a ton of improvement that there is to be made on my end and on our team's end, but just excited to be back on the floor."

It had been more than 400 days since Haliburton's last NBA game, when he tore his right Achilles during Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals. He struggled to sleep last night, but he said that had more to do with the anticipation of playing his first game back at Iowa State, where he played for two years in college from 2018 to 2020.

The Pacers had initially scheduled this game for the 2025 preseason, but with Haliburton sidelined last season, the game got pushed back one year.

Haliburton wanted to replicate a college atmosphere Wednesday night, so he bought out the student section at both ends of the arena, so seats were available to students on a first come, first serve basis, prompting a line that wrapped around the block of the arena hours before tipoff. The fans at the front of the line said they began lining up at 11 p.m. the night before.

"It's the loudest preseason game I've ever been a part of," Haliburton said. "But had a lot of fun, a lot of special memories I've made here and that just adds to it."

Haliburton played all of his 16 minutes during the first half, but fans inside Hilton Coliseum wanted more of the Pacers star.

With Haliburton sitting on the bench during the fourth quarter, fans began to chant "We want Hali."

Haliburton responded by pointing to his feet. His basketball shoes had been left in the locker room, and he was wearing white sandals and socks, a signal that he was done for the night.

"Put your shoes on," the next chant began. Haliburton laughed after the game and said he wasn't tempted.

"Hell no," Haliburton said after the game with a laugh. "I appreciate that the students wanted that as they should, but we have a process."

stories.headline: NFL, union clarify celebration rules, OK drinking gestures
stories.summary: The NFL and NFLPA said recent player celebrations imitating drinking a beverage will no longer be violations or result in discipline. The sides also clarified what celebrations remain prohibited.
stories.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- The NFL and NFLPA announced in a joint statement Wednesday that recent player celebrations imitating drinking a beverage will no longer be violations or result in discipline.

In Week 2, multiple players, including 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk, Colts guard Matt Goncalves and Cowboys tight end Jake Ferguson, were fined after performing celebrations in which they mimicked drinking a beverage of some kind.

An appeals officer rescinded the fines for Juszczyk and Ferguson earlier Wednesday as the league and players' association worked out a solution to solve any future issues on the matter.

"The league-wide guidance provides players with greater clarity on how they can celebrate while remaining within the rules," the statement said.

As part of that clarification, the following celebrations remain prohibited and can result in a 15-yard unsportsmanlike penalty, a fine or both:

• Gestures that depict violence, including the use of guns or other weapons or gang-related signs

• Gestures that depict smoking or drug use

• Gestures that are sexual in nature

Also included in the resolved guidelines is a note that when conduct falls into a "gray area," the league will contact the player before imposing any discipline that may require an appeal.

According NFLPA executive director JC Tretter, there were 20 celebration fines in Weeks 2 and 3, which he called "an unusual spike." Tretter wrote on X that all of those fined players appealed, with some already overturned.

"We raised this issue and pushed for greater clarity around what will and won't result in discipline," Tretter wrote. "When something falls into a gray area, communication and education should come before punishment. We're glad the league will seek to educate players before immediately defaulting to a fine."

A league source said the NFL and the NFLPA worked together to address the issue over the past couple of weeks before releasing the joint statement Wednesday.

When informed of the changes, Juszczyk and his teammates said they were happy to hear that he will be able to continue what has been his signature celebration.

"I guess I've got to start thinking of my celebrations for this week pertaining to drinks," linebacker Fred Warner said Wednesday, laughing. "It is great for Juice because he's been doing that same celebration for years. But yeah, man, just try to have a little fun out there. That's what the league's about."
